title: Can a mean be bigger than every value in the data?
description: Nine days of tap water usage are used to ask whether the mean or the median can lie between twenty five and thirty litres. The video uses the fair share meaning of the mean and the middle meaning of the median.
teaching_notes: One idea: the mean and the median always lie between the smallest and the largest value. Watch for students who think a mean can be larger than every value if the data is spread out.

source: Daily water usage from a tap: can the mean or median lie between 25 and 30, or beyond the smallest and largest values
video_script.why: The child can find a mean and a median and now uses what they mean to say where they can and cannot lie.
video_script.substitution: Nine bars of water are levelled to the same height, which gives the mean, and the middle bar after sorting gives the median.
video_script.anchor: Water used in litres on nine days: 5.6, 8, 3.09, 12.9, 6.5, 12.1, 11.3, 20.5, 7.4.
video_script.payoff_line: No, the mean and the median both stay between the smallest and the largest value.

final_answer.value: No: mean 9.71 litres and median 8 litres, both between 3.09 and 20.5
final_answer.spoken: mean nine point seven one litres and median eight litres

maths_rules: levelling cannot make any bar taller than the tallest or shorter than the shortest, so smallest <= mean <= largest
video_script.design: One idea: the mean is a level, the median is a middle. Nine water bars sit in the anchor; they level out on the board and a band marks the smallest to the largest.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book about water used from a tap.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>It was measured on nine days, and the board shows each day.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The smallest was about three litres. The largest was twenty point five litres.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Can the mean or the median lie between twenty five and thirty litres?

marks.m1: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Think and tell.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>The mean is the fair share. It is the level every day would have if the water were shared equally.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The median is the middle value once the days are sorted.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Given, the water used on nine days.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The smallest is three point zero nine litres and the largest is twenty point five litres.

beats.on_screen: To find: can the mean or median lie between 25 and 30? Can either go below the smallest or above the largest?
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to find where the mean and the median can lie.

marks.m2: the fifth bar glows with four bars on each side

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, sort the nine usages from smallest to largest.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The middle one is the fifth, with four days on each side.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>It is eight litres, so the median is eight litres.

beats.on_screen: levelling the bars: no bar ends taller than 20.5 or shorter than 3.09

marks.m1: water moves from the tall bars to the short bars
marks.m2: a band from 3.09 to 20.5 appears around the level

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, level the bars by moving water from tall bars to short bars.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>No bar can end taller than the tallest one, or shorter than the shortest.
The level is the mean, so the mean stays inside that band.

marks.m1: the nine usages are added to 87.39

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, add the nine usages to see the actual mean.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The total is eighty seven point three nine litres, shared equally among nine days.

beats.on_screen: Check: the median is one of the middle values, so 3.09 ≤ median ≤ 20.5

marks.m1: the median 8 sits inside the band
marks.m2: the band from 25 to 30 is marked far to the right

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, check the median against the same band.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The median is one of the sorted values. It cannot leave the range from smallest to largest.

beats.on_screen: Answer: No. mean ≈ 9.71 litres, median 8 litres, both between 3.09 and 20.5

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>No, the mean and the median both stay between the smallest and the largest value.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Here the mean is about nine point seven one litres, and the median is eight litres.
